trials.notes: Used the correct structural parser (`WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment`) and only documented methods: `next_tag`, `get_current_depth`, `next_token`, `get_token_type`, and `get_modifiable_text`. The depth-bounded token walk and `#text` guard match the documented subtree text recipe. Handles decoded text and empty text content correctly.

Essentially matches the canonical documented pattern: find the first `H1`, record depth, walk tokens while still inside that subtree, append only `#text` via decoded `get_modifiable_text()`. No undocumented APIs or `_doing_it_wrong` records.

Correct processor choice and fully documented API surface. The implementation follows the HTML Processor docs under the subtree text extraction recipe and respects the important edge distinction between no `H1` (`null`) and an `H1` with no text (`''`).

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 8 hidden cases, so there were no failed-case misconceptions to attribute. The rendered docs did well on the exact pressure points for this task: `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor` > `Which processor should I use?` explicitly says collecting element text and handling missing closing tags require `WP_HTML_Processor`; `WP_HTML_Processor` > `Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree` gives the same depth-bounded `next_token()` plus `#text` plus `get_modifiable_text()` pattern; `next_token()` explains that unguarded token walks continue past the original element and must be bounded by depth or breadcrumbs; `get_modifiable_text()` explains it is decoded text but not itself a predicate for ordinary text nodes. Near-miss: the candidates did not check `paused_at_incomplete_token()` or `get_last_error()`, but for this read-only extraction contract the expected `unclosed-h1` behavior is best-effort text, and the docs explicitly frame incomplete-source handling as caller policy rather than mandatory rejection.

doc_gaps.location: WP_HTML_Processor::get_modifiable_text / Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The docs imply decoded plaintext through examples and comparison guidance, but the return-value contract for ordinary `#text` tokens could be more explicit at the method heading.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a concise sentence to the method docblock: for `#text`, this returns decoded text content suitable for DOM-style text extraction; serialized HTML should use `serialize_token()` instead.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs correctly say incomplete-source handling is caller policy, but readers must combine that with text-extraction guidance to know best-effort read-only extraction may still return accumulated text.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short read-only example or note stating that accumulated `#text` already visited remains valid even if a later incomplete token pauses the parser, and callers decide whether to reject or return the partial text.
